rewrite.explanation: existsSync stats the path synchronously and returns true or false; it never returns contents or size and, unlike the fs.promises API, involves no Promise. Checking first and acting later leaves a window in which the file can change, so for reads it is usually better to attempt the operation and handle ENOENT.

rationale: Simple, correct recall of a non-deprecated API; the rewrite adds the caveat that gives it engineering value.
evidence: node: existsSync(existingFile) → true; existsSync(missingPath) → false; typeof → "boolean"; instanceof Promise → false

rewrite.question: Which call removes one specific listener that was added earlier with .on?
rewrite.hint: You must pass the same function reference you registered; the emitter can only detach what it can match. Recall which method pairs with .on for that.
options: emitter.stop("evt", fn)
emitter.off("evt", fn)
emitter.delete("evt", fn)
emitter.clear("evt", fn)
rewrite.explanation: emitter.off("evt", fn), an alias of removeListener, detaches that exact function from that event; the emitter compares references, so an anonymous inline listener cannot be removed later. removeAllListeners("evt") drops every listener at once; stop, delete and clear do not exist on EventEmitter. Removing listeners when a component or connection goes away prevents leaks and the MaxListenersExceeded warning.

rationale: Cleanup is the half of the subscription pattern learners forget, so the objective is worth keeping; the odd-one-out key format and filler hint are fixable.
evidence: node: after on(fn) listenerCount 1; off("evt", fn) → 0; removeListener → 0; EventEmitter.prototype.off === EventEmitter.prototype.removeListener → true
